title: Giving
hook: Catholics support the Church and the poor from what they have
tomorrow: why does owing weigh so much, even when the number is small?

segments.voice: Yesterday, without work: men no one had hired, paid a full day anyway. The line was worth isn't a job.

The first paycheck lands, and before the excitement wears off, the math starts: phone bill, gas, savings, the thing waiting in the cart. The Bible's old answer to how much to give has a name. In Genesis, Abram gives the priest Melchisedech a tenth of everything. Later, the law of Moses calls that tenth of the harvest a tithe and says it is holy to the Lord.
screen: `THE FIRST PAYCHECK.` → `ABRAM GIVES A TENTH.` → `HOLY TO THE LORD.`

segments.voice: So does the Church require exactly a tenth? Not by its own law. Among the precepts of the Church, the Catechism lists helping to provide for the Church's needs, each according to their own ability. No fixed number. What scripture keeps coming back to is the order. Proverbs, in the Douay-Rheims: "Honour the Lord with thy substance, and give him of the first of all thy fruits." The first, not the leftovers. And the spirit of it: Paul tells the Corinthians that each should give as they've decided in their heart, not sadly or because they have to, "for God loveth a cheerful giver." Now look back over two weeks. A road walked with eyes up, a first task offered, a noon pause, a slump outlasted, a door, a table, a look back at night, a day handed over. Then work as creation, work done well, colleagues, both sides of the deal, and worth that isn't a job. Giving is where it all comes back around: what the work earned, offered first.
screen: `NO FIXED NUMBER IN THE PRECEPT.` · `THE FIRST OF ALL THY FRUITS.` · `A CHEERFUL GIVER.` · `TWO WEEKS, COMING BACK AROUND.` · then, large: `GIVE FIRST.`

segments.voice: Pick an amount that's honest for you, any amount, and decide where it will go: your parish, a food pantry, someone you know who's in need. Write it down with the day you'll give it, and put it above every other line in your budget.
Tithe. In the Bible, the tenth set aside as holy; in Catholic practice, a share given first, by each one's means.
Your line: give first, from the top and gladly, before the bills. Two weeks of ordinary holiness, done.
